newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices mixed - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices mixed - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were mixed, with weakness in the western Corn Belt tied to increased marketings, livestock dealers said.
Hog price strength in the eastern belt was tied to strong interest from an area packer planning a large Saturday slaughter, sources there said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower at $50.00 to $50.50 in the country and $51.50 at plants. Illinois hogs sold steady at $50.00 to $50.50 in the country and $50.50 to $51.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $51.50 to $52.00 at plants amid strong packer interest, they said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $48.50 to $49.00 in the country and $50.00 to $51.00 at plants.

Some weakness in the western Corn Belt also was tied to IBP's announcement earlier this week that it would cut the second shift on Monday at its Columbus Junction, Iowa, hog plant for an indefinite period.
Declines could be muted by a snowstorm in western Iowa, which could limit hog marketings, dealers said.
